store-corrupt-dismiss-overwrites-as-ship: FND-06: the TS notices store replaced a corrupt steam_engine_notices.json on the first dismissal with a fresh document holding only the new key and left no copy of the corrupt bytes. The Rust port opens the file only through the StoreHost, which refuses a file that is not a JSON object and never overwrites it, so a corrupt notices file is kept byte for byte on every read and every write. A dismissal it could not record answers {ok: false} (the TS answered {ok: true}) and creates nothing; every notice reads as not dismissed until the user repairs or removes the file. The golden's storeFile and ok therefore differ on purpose, and the replay asserts the kept file and the refusal instead.
publisher-throws: The TS publisher was a function that could throw (a renderer push that failed), and recordLaunchDecision and the three notices caught it, logged 'engine state publisher failed' and answered false or published nothing. The Rust push goes through FrontendEmitter::emit, which returns nothing and cannot fail, so there is no failure to catch and no log line to write: a launch always records and publishes, and an overlay, exit or deadline notice answers true as soon as a state was published for the title. The golden's five logged errors and its five false answers are not reproducible, and the replay asserts the shared sequence number across the launch, overlay, exit and deadline notices instead, which is the behaviour the case existed to pin.
a-corrupt-notices-file-leaves-one-copy-o: The StoreHost, which owns every store file (Phase 85), keeps one '<name>.corrupt.<stamp>.json' copy of the bytes of a store file it cannot read as a JSON object, and leaves the original untouched. The TS notices store read a corrupt file in place and made no copy, so the profile tree of a case that seeds a corrupt notices file differs by that one file. The copy is made once per process (the port remembers a refused open instead of retrying it on every state read), and the replay asserts exactly one copy in each corrupt case and drops it from the tree it compares; the original file is compared byte for byte.
a-notices-file-the-host-wrote-is-0600: The TS CacheStore rewrote a notices file in place, so a file the case seeded at 0644 stayed 0644 after a dismissal. The StoreHost writes a user-state store atomically with owner-only bits (0600 file, 0700 directories it creates), so a notices file the port wrote is 0600 whatever mode it started with, and a file only read keeps the mode it was seeded with. The mode is a tightening, not a behaviour the game page can see, so the replay compares the notices file's kind and bytes against the golden and asserts the mode separately: 0600 in every case whose golden recorded a successful dismissal.
